title: The Georgia Guidestones: The Elite Have a Laugh
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the Georgia Guidestones, granite monuments erected in 1979-1980 near Elberton, Georgia, inscribed with ten guidelines in eight languages. They cover the commission by the pseudonymous R.C. Christian, the banker Wyatt Martin and granite finisher Joe Finley, the stones' astronomical features, the inscriptions and their eugenics and population-control overtones, theories linking the Rosicrucians, Ted Turner, Freemasons and Herbert Kirsten, conspiracy theories and vandalism, and the 2022 bombing that destroyed the monument. The episode closes with listener mail about breakfast foods and brunch.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to the Georgia Guidestones
segments.summary: The hosts joke about never visiting the Georgia Guidestones, call them America's Stonehenge, and preview the history and inscriptions.

segments.title: R.C. Christian arrives in Elberton
segments.summary: R.C. Christian, a pseudonymous well-dressed stranger, approaches Elberton's granite industry. Joe Finley agrees to build the monument at a high price, and banker Wyatt Martin agrees to finance it on condition of secrecy.

segments.title: Construction, land purchase and civic pride
segments.summary: Christian gives Finley a model and instructions, and the project requires deep excavation and a large crane. Five acres are bought from a local landowner, and the county takes pride in the project. Some locals worry about occult associations.

segments.title: Dedication, dimensions and astronomical features
segments.summary: The stones were dedicated March 22, two days after the spring equinox. Each stone is about nineteen feet tall, weighs around 120 tons, and has about 4,000 letters. The monument works as a clock, calendar and compass, with sightlines for solstices and the North Star.

segments.title: The ten guidelines and their languages
segments.summary: The hosts read the inscriptions in eight languages, including the ten guides on population, reproduction, a world court, a living language, and leaving room for nature. They discuss the Cold War context and the population scare.

segments.title: Rosicrucians, Thomas Paine and conspiracy associations
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Rosicrucians and Thomas Paine's Age of Reason as connections people draw to the stones, and how the monument drew fundamentalist and conspiracy interest, including a 2000s minister calling it the Antichrist's commandments.

segments.title: Ted Turner, Freemasons and the suspects
segments.summary: Ted Turner is considered as a suspect because of his Turner Doomsday video and UN donation, but the hosts dismiss him because his link is only proximity. Freemasons are mentioned as common conspiracy targets in Elberton.

segments.title: Psychology of conspiracy theorists and the identity of R.C. Christian
segments.summary: The hosts reflect on why conspiracy theories attract believers. They then discuss a documentary identifying Herbert Kirsten of Fort Dodge, Iowa, as possibly R.C. Christian, citing his correspondence with Wyatt Martin and his political views.

segments.title: Vandalism, the 2022 bombing and the monument's demise
segments.summary: The stones suffered vandalism from the mid-2000s. A bomb in July 2022 destroyed much of the monument, and the county voted to demolish the remains and not rebuild. Investigations by the ATF and GBI are ongoing.

segments.title: Listener mail: breakfast foods and brunch
segments.summary: Listeners write about full English breakfast and whether a nine a.m. brunch counts as brunch. The hosts rule it is breakfast.
